source.title: Scaling an Autoregressive Transformer for Single-Cell Generation
source.authors: Aleksandr Sharipov; Yusif Mukhtarov; Igor Molybog

record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling behavior in a new setting: an RQ-VAE-tokenized single-cell transformer trained on gene-expression data, rather than a language model trained on text.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a fitted loss law, held-out loss predictions, a compute-optimal frontier, and generation-quality results. It also reports loss trajectories under different sampling schemes and on a perturbation-benchmark holdout; these are recorded as findings that do not directly test a listed version. Comparisons to other papers in Table 2 and the related-work discussion are not this study's own results.
record.test_reason: The study fits a joint power law L(N,D) to held-out pretraining loss of a single-cell (RQ-VAE-tokenized) transformer over an independent 22-point N×D grid. It predicts four held-out runs, derives a compute-optimal frontier, and correlates a generation-quality task with pretraining loss. This is a new setting with its own results on V2, V3, V5 and V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that the plateaus other single-cell studies report reflect a model-size bottleneck, or limits on downstream tasks, rather than an absence of pretraining-loss data scaling. They state the generation-quality probe is within-run at one model size and not a downstream scaling result. Their claim that quality improves 'monotonically' is not fully supported by Table 4.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the Chinchilla Approach-3 parametric fit and cross-entropy loss, but applies them to an RQ-VAE-tokenized single-cell transformer, with data counted in expression vectors rather than language-model tokens.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported controlled sampling comparison shows different validation-loss trajectories under proportional versus uniform cell-type pool sampling. The authors state that absolute losses across these sampling runs are not comparable.

fits_no_version.finding: Held-out loss on perturbation-benchmark control cells falls early, then rises to finish above its start, at every grid size. Meanwhile scBaseCount validation loss keeps falling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining loss on a composition-mismatched narrow distribution can worsen with continued training while the in-distribution loss follows the scaling law.

fits_no_version.finding: Uniform cell-type pool sampling causes validation loss to flatten near 3.54 and then rise to 3.61 while training loss keeps falling. Proportional sampling shows no such divergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The data sampling scheme determines whether the measured loss reflects data scaling or memorization, which bears on how β is read.

record.problems: The model-size range is 1.3–83.9M parameters and the authors say they cannot rule out exponent changes at much larger scales. The fitted law is for one architecture family and one single-cell pretraining objective. Generation-quality tracking is measured at one model size. No uncertainty intervals are reported for the fitted exponents or the held-out predictions.

untested.parts: Language-model held-out loss. Only a single-cell transformer is studied, so its power-law loss is evidence for V5, not V1.

Extrapolation by orders of magnitude. Held-out D reaches 1.01B against a fit maximum of 362M (~3x). All held-out runs use model sizes inside the fitted range, so there is no extrapolation in N beyond 83.9M.

Measured compute-optimal points (isoFLOP or envelope methods). The frontier is obtained only by analytically inverting the fitted form, so 'stable power of compute' follows from the fit, not from an independent test.
Entire version. Width/depth ratio is fixed across sizes.
Image, video, repeated-data, fine-tuning and transfer regimes. Also continuous-embedding single-cell models.
Downstream performance across model sizes, and perturbation-response tasks. Generation quality is measured only across checkpoints of one 4.43M model.
No comparison of fitting methods, parameter counting or schedules. The multi-start sensitivity is mentioned but alternate fits are not reported.

missing.what: The authors argue that a fixed-N slice of the fitted surface plateaus in D, which they say explains other studies' 'no data scaling' results. This is derived from the fit, not from a separate measurement.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Rows are linked to V2 and V3 because those versions do not name a modality; V1 explicitly concerns language models. The held-out N values are all at or below the fitted range, and the D extrapolation is ~3x, so the V2 support is narrow. No uncertainty intervals are given for the exponents. The authors note that Approach-3 fits are sensitive to initialization.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test language-model held-out loss scaling in parameters, tokens, or compute.
Predictions are tested on held-out single-cell runs, not on language-model runs or runs orders of magnitude larger.
The data quantity is single-cell vectors, not language-model training tokens; the paper does not test language-model compute-optimal allocation.
Network shape is held fixed across sizes; depth, width, and other architecture details are not varied at fixed parameter count.
Only this single-cell, discrete-tokenization architecture and its pretraining regime are tested; image, video, repeated-data scaling laws, fine-tuning, and transfer scaling are not tested.
Generation quality is evaluated at checkpoints of one model size; perturbation-response task performance and downstream scaling across model sizes are not tested.
The study does not compare fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits across fitting methods or setups. A multi-start fit is used, but alternate fitted laws are not reported.

rows.subject: RQ-VAE-tokenized causal transformer (22-point grid aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Jointly varies model parameters N and training data D and fits a two-term loss law.
rows.measure: Held-out next-token cross-entropy as a function of N and D
rows.value: L(N,D) = 2.90 + 2.05 × 10^4/N^0.81 + 4.28 × 10^3/D^0.57; R² = 0.977 on loss and 0.976 on log-loss; log-loss RMSE = 0.0046; mean absolute error = 0.008 nats
rows.note: The authors report both fitted exponents as positive and say the residuals show no systematic trend with N or D.

rows.subject: RQ-VAE-tokenized causal transformer (fitted compute-optimal frontier)
rows.operation_detail: Inverts the fitted loss law using the compute proxy C ≈ 6ND to obtain the loss-minimizing allocation.
rows.measure: Compute-optimal model size and data allocation
rows.note: The fitted frontier allocates compute more quickly to data than to parameters in the tested regime.

rows.subject: RQ-VAE-tokenized causal transformer, N = 1.31M
rows.operation_detail: Predicts a held-out run's loss using the fitted scaling law.
rows.note: The paper says this point tests interpolation.
rows.check: The note says the paper calls this point the interpolation test. The paper never says which of the four held-out points is the interpolation one. D=19.7M is also below the grid's 38.1M minimum, so attributing interpolation to r3 is unsupported.

source_check.correct: N=1.31M, D=19.7M; predicted loss 3.4245, measured loss 3.4357, reported error +0.33%. The paper does not identify which held-out point tests interpolation; this D is below the fit's 38.1M minimum. State: observed for V5; cannot_determine for V2's orders-of-magnitude extrapolation.
source_check.problem: The interpolation note is unsupported, and the run does not test prediction at orders-of-magnitude larger scale.

rows.subject: 4.43M-parameter model (ten-checkpoint aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Correlates generation-quality metrics across ten checkpoints with validation cross-entropy.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation of mean-expression Pearson with validation loss; correlation of mean-expression MAE with validation loss
rows.value: r = −0.99 for mean-expression Pearson; r = +0.98 for mean-expression MAE
rows.note: The authors say generation quality improves monotonically as validation loss falls; no correlation is reported for discriminability.
rows.check: The authors' claim of monotonic improvement is not fully borne out by Table 4. Discriminability dips at steps 7,350, 10,290 and 14,700, and MAE ties or rises at 10,290. No correlation is reported for discriminability.
